instruction: On slide 2, make the title italic and change its font size to 36 points.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 2, opened View > Notes to add 'Team Members' as a note, then selected the title text and applied bold formatting. Completed in 15 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Impress slides, use View menu to access Notes view, type text in notes area, select title text, and apply font formatting (bold). Familiar with text selection and formatting toolbar.
metadata.task_rationale: Original task tested bold formatting and notes. This variation tests italic formatting and font size change — same interaction pattern (select title, modify font properties) but different properties.
metadata.explanation: Task requires making slide 2 title italic and changing font size to 36pt. Getter extracts italic and size properties from the title placeholder on slide 2. Metric awards 0.5 for correct italic, 0.5 for correct size (with 1pt tolerance).

scoring_breakdown.italic: 0.5 - Title text is set to italic

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets slide 2 (index 1, 0-based) and finds the title placeholder (idx==0), extracting italic and size_pt properties from the first non-empty run.
EMU to point conversion (/ 12700) is correct for python-pptx font.size values.
Metric correctly accesses expected rules directly (expected.get('expected_italic'), expected.get('expected_size_pt')) without wrapping — proper handling for expected.type='rule'.
Both instruction requirements (italic + font size 36pt) are fully covered with appropriate partial credit (0.5 each).
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring getter reads the latest state.

Minor concern: run.font.italic can return None (inherited) rather than True. If italic is inherited from a higher level, the comparison None == True would incorrectly fail. In practice, explicit user action sets italic at the run level, so this is unlikely to cause issues.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider handling the case where run.font.italic returns None (inherited italic) by checking the effective italic state, e.g., treating None as potentially inherited from paragraph or slide master styles.
